label: 1e-6 as a double, not a float
round the intermediate product to float
replace:
float t = ppmScale * ppm;
	timingOffset = t * 1e-6f;
why: F6000 recorded this as 'a REAL gap...closable by a search for a separating pair' and left it open. Compiled both spellings under the exact period toolchain (dsplibs-tc342, -O3 -frename-registers -march=i386 -mtune=i686 -mfpmath=387 -mno-ieee-fp -fomit-frame-pointer -maccumulate-outgoing-args) and disassembled the result: GCC 3.4.2 never stores the intermediate `t` to memory -- both spellings compile to the IDENTICAL three instructions (flds/fmuls/fmuls/ret), because with no -ffloat-store a local float that never escapes stays on the x87 stack at full extended precision regardless of its declared type, so the explicit intermediate variable never actually narrows anything. Also swept ~20,000,000 random (ppmScale, ppm) float pairs through both compiled functions (excluding NaN/Inf) with zero divergent results, confirming byte-identical FP output as well as byte-identical code. The search F6000 asked for was run; it found none because none exists under this compiler.
